sources.entry: flowctl - Self-service workflow execution platform with approvals, remote execution and scheduling. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: flowctl is an open-source self-service platform that gives users secure access to multi-step workflows, distributed as a single binary.
summary.what_it_does: Flowctl lets users run predefined workflows defined in YAML or HUML config, with inputs, actions, and approval steps. Workflows can run actions through executors such as docker, as the README's example shows, and can execute on remote nodes over SSH. It provides OIDC-based SSO, teams with isolated namespaces and built-in RBAC, encrypted storage for SSH keys and other secrets, streaming real-time logs of executions, and cron-based scheduling. The README says the executor paradigm makes it domain-agnostic, so workflows can cover tasks such as granting SSH access, provisioning infrastructure, or custom business process automation.
use_cases: self-service access to servers via SSH
how_to_run: Download the latest binary from releases
Alternatively, use the provided docker-compose.yml file
notable: Workflows defined in simple YAML or HUML config
Encrypted secret storage for SSH keys and passwords
caveats: Docker is listed as a prerequisite
Full documentation is hosted externally at flowctl.net
